features.headline: Which NBA players have the most triple-doubles of all time?
features.desc: Russell Westbrook holds the NBA record for most triple-doubles in a career. See who else joins him on the list.
body: Russell Westbrook has more than earned the nickname Mr. Triple Double.
In basketball, a triple-double is when a player compiles a double-digit total in three of five statistical categories (assists, blocks, points, rebounds and steals) over the course of a game.
Blocks and steals were officially recorded by the NBA starting in the 1973-74 season. No player in NBA history has recorded more triple-doubles than Westbrook.
On May 10, 2021, Westbrook became the NBA's career leader in triple-doubles, tallying 28 points, 13 rebounds and 21 assists for the Washington Wizards in a 125-124 loss against the Atlanta Hawks.
It marked the 182nd triple-double of Westbrook's career, passing Oscar Robertson for the most on the all-time list.
Nikola Jokić also has since passed Robertson, whose record stood for more than 47 years.
Westbrook had already broken Robertson's record for the most triple-doubles in a single NBA season (41), recording 42 during the 2016-17 campaign.

features.headline: Rams take Packers' dinner in first Thanksgiving Eve game
features.desc: The night was full of interceptions and injuries with the Rams taking the W.
body: INGLEWOOD, Calif. — In the week leading up to the Rams' 26-13 victory over the Green Bay Packers, the mindset in the Los Angeles locker room was to treat this Thanksgiving Eve matchup as a playoff game.

Both teams entered the game at 6-4, likely competing with the 6-4 Seattle Seahawks for the final NFC wild-card spot. And because of the head-to-head tiebreaker that would go to the winner, the game had a 39% swing in playoff chances.
According to ESPN Analytics, that was the second highest of any Week 12 game.

The Rams, who entered the game with a 45% chance to make the playoffs, now have a 55% chance, according to ESPN Analytics. Their chances would have fallen to 25% with a loss. And while the Rams have won five games in a row, they entered the contest with the hardest remaining schedule in the NFL.
The Rams (7-4) now sit in second place in the NFC West behind the 9-1 San Francisco 49ers.
Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

Most surprising performance: Rams running back Blake Corum ran for a career-high 32 times, finishing with 184 yards and a touchdown. He also had two catches for 21 yards. It was his second straight game with 100 or more rushing yards.
He had one such game in his first 43 career games, according to ESPN Research. Corum played 52 offensive snaps (73.2%) compared to Williams' 36 snaps (50.7%).
Williams was added to the injury report this week with what McVay called soreness in his toe.
Trend to watch: The Rams got bad injury news for their tight end Monday, when head coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson would likely need season-ending surgery on the ankle he injured in Week 3.

Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

Skubal to NYM | Peralta to BAL Sato to CHC | Gray to MIN | Bauers to BOS

It's been three seasons of injuries and subpar results since Luis Robert Jr. had his big year in 2023 for the Chicago White Sox, when he hit.264 with 38 home runs, 75 extra-base hits and plus defense in center field.

Yet we still dream the magic will somehow return, even as he now enters his age-29 season. The Baltimore Orioles are certainly dreaming big, believing Robert can be their full-time center fielder in 2027.
The best guess here: It's unlikely to happen. There's nothing from the past three seasons that suggests Robert can stay healthy and also hit the way he did in 2023.
Over the past three seasons, averaging 90 games per season, he has hit.223/.290/.379 for a subpar OPS+ of 88.
That includes three games in 2026 with the Orioles, who claimed him off waivers from the Mets in August — only to see Robert immediately go down with a hamstring injury.

That didn't scare them off. Look, Robert is enticing. He still has power and is still capable of playing at least a decent center field — two attributes the Orioles didn't get from their center fielders in 2026.

features.headline: VAR review: Why Man United should've gotten winner vs. Sporting
features.desc: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
body: The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.
Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship.

With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday.
Referee: Szymon Marciniak VAR: Piotr Lasyk Time: 80 minutes Incident: Sporting's Luis Suárez challenged United goalkeeper Senne Lammens as he attempted to catch a high ball.

The United keeper then dropped the ball under the pressure of Suárez, with the Sporting attacker helping himself to the loose ball and scoring his second goal of the night. The on-field decision was a goal.
VAR Decision: VAR checked and cleared the on-field decision, and the goal stood.
VAR Review: VAR were very comfortable that no offense had been committed by the Sporting attacker and cleared the on-field decision as correct.
Verdict / Insight: It was a correct call by the on-field referee to allow the goal and an equally correct non-intervention from VAR.

features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
Outfielder Luis Robert Jr. and the Baltimore Orioles are in agreement on a one-year, $12 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Left-hander David Peterson and the Colorado Rockies are in agreement on a two-year, $32 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Right-hander Kevin Gausman and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a one-year, $25 million contract, pending physical, sources tell ESPN.
Catcher Gary Sanchez and the Miami Marlins are in agreement on a one-year, $6.5 million contract, a source tells ESPN.
Left-handed reliever JoJo Romero and the San Diego Padres are in agreement on a free agent contract, a source tells ESPN.
Third baseman Alec Bohm has agreed to a two-year deal with the Kansas City Royals, according to multiple reports.
Right-hander Freddy Peralta and the Baltimore Orioles are in agreement on a five-year, $125 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Left-hander Kris Bubic and the Cleveland Guardians are in agreement on a one-year, $17.5 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
The Chicago Cubs have reached an agreement with Japanese Central League MVP Teruaki Sato on a six-year, $120 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
